newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open firmer on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open firmer on selective buying.

text.p: Singapore shares opened firmer on Tuesday correcting slightly the big slump on Monday which sent the market to an 18-month low, dealers said.
The Straits Times Industrial Index at 0130 GMT rose 13.31 points or 0.65 percent to 2,058.89 points.
The market picked up due to buying of some index-linked stocks this morning, one dealer at a local brokerage firm said.
"The market is still in a corrective mode and could come down some more as the 2,045 mark was breached," the dealer said.
The STII fell 31.07 points or 1.5 percent to 2045.58 points on Monday.
Dealers said the rise was led by buying of selected property stocks. Total volume was thin with 6.18 million shares traded. Gainers were ahead of losers 52 to 51.
City Develoment and Singapore Press foreign led the gainers, putting on 20 cents.
Bukit Sembawang headed the losers down 30 cents. The counter was the top loser on Monday shedding a S$1.00 drop on trade of two lots. Berger International lost 20 cents with 30,000 shares traded.
